messages:
nina_p: Heads-up — we need to pick a default client-visible status when we early-shed. Current options: 429 (rate limited) vs 503 (service unavailable). Thoughts? We also need headers for telemetry and client backoff.

sam_h: I lean 429 for per-key burst hits (client exceeded burst credits). 503 makes more sense for global capacity or infra retries.

josh_k: Agree. 429 -> include Retry-After and burst headers so smart clients can back off gracefully. 503 -> indicates something wrong on our side, clients should probably pause and alert.

leah_m: Note: some HTTP libraries automatically retry on 503s and not on 429s. That behavior affects which status we choose for soft-shed vs hard failure.

nina_p: What if we add an explicit header `X-Redwood-Action` with values `shed|queue|degraded` so clients can make informed decisions? Also add `X-Redwood-Burst-Remaining` and `X-Redwood-Burst-Window`.

sam_h: Example headers I'd like: `X-Redwood-Action: shed`, `Retry-After: 2`, `X-Redwood-Burst-Remaining: 0`, `X-Redwood-Burst-Window: 60` (seconds).

josh_k: We should distinguish two code paths: precheck failures (reject before enqueue -> 429) vs in-flight aborts (accepted then later aborted -> 503). That maps nicely to client semantics.

leah_m: Router change: precheck token credits + tenant concurrency -> if fail, immediate 429 + headers. If request hits queue then OOM/failure downstream -> 503. Keep logic simple.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled to staging @15:00 with header prototype and telemetry hooks. Deploy details: <https://ci/redeploy/123|deploy-123>.

nina_p: For Retry-After units we'll keep seconds. If we need sub-second precision we can add `X-Redwood-Retry-Millis`.

sam_h: Telemetry: tag metrics with `shed_reason=(burst|fairness|region)` and `action=(429|503)`. Dashboards: per-org shed-rate + top endpoints by shed_count.

josh_k: Console UX: under Quotas show "Burst credits" with current window, remaining credits, and a "Projected shed rate" sparkline. Add a simulation toggler to preview increases to reserved capacity.

leah_m: Mobile SDKs often do exponential retry on 503 but not 429. We must publish SDK guidance and update client libs: `if 429 -> respect Retry-After; if 503 -> exponential with jitter`. Consider an optional header `X-Redwood-Suggested-Backoff: exp/200/10000` (format: method/base_ms/max_ms).

nina_p: I like `X-Redwood-Backoff: exp/200/10000` as a compact signal. Not prescriptive but helpful.

sam_h: Server-side preference: early-shed to 429 for predictable behavior on per-org burst breaches. Use 503 for system-level overloads. We'll document the difference.

leah_m: Also add trace tag `shed.sample=1` and `shed.reason` to link sheds to traces. That will make postmortems easier.

josh_k: Quick client pseudo: ```python
if resp.status_code == 429:
    wait = resp.headers.get('Retry-After') or default
    sleep(wait)
elif resp.status_code == 503:
    sleep(exponential_jitter())
```

nina_p: I'll draft an RFC with header names, status semantics, telemetry keys, and console mocks. @sam_h @leah_m can you add metric names and a first-pass grafana query? Need UX copy too.

sam_h: Will add metrics: `redwood_shed_total{reason="burst",org="..."}`, `redwood_burst_remaining{org="..."}` and example PromQL for 5m rate. I'll upload panel JSON after RFC.

leah_m: I'll draft console copy: "Requests above burst credits will be shed with 429. Consider increasing reserved capacity or smoothing client traffic. See suggested backoff in headers"

infra-bot: Staging deploy succeeded :white_check_mark: (build 123, pods rolled). Logs: <https://logs/123|view>.

nina_p: Thanks all. RFC will land in #eng-platform-docs in ~1hr. Plan to gate the prod flip behind a feature flag + canary for a few customer orgs next week.
